This is the heavy step, and it is yours to carry — not the user's. If the code
does not run in isolation, **build the test doubles or emulators needed to run

settles.

  languages, write a small emitter by hand following the same shape.

  exposes a step listener / observer / middleware hook, register on it — that

  Code authored through this toolchain always has one

  capture easier — that changes the thing under audit. (If you are separately
  fixing or authoring code in that repo, `docs/capture-ready.md` is what to

  no-op window). Use existing test doubles or emulators.

  contract declares but the corpus never visits is a capture bug until proven
  otherwise (too-coarse polling, a scenario you didn't drive) — not evidence
  the state is rare. Step 3's `mutate.mjs --all` makes this check mechanical:

> [`docs/diagrams/index.dc.html`](docs/diagrams/index.dc.html). ## How it works

Everything revolves around three artifacts you can read and diff: 1. **A contract** (`contract.json`) — what's observable: the state fields that matter, the actions the machine accepts, the data each action can carry, which states are terminal. This is the scope of the audit. 2. **A spec** — an executable model of your code, written by an LLM from your source. By default it's a strict, self-describing state-machine module (the [SAM pattern](https://sam.js.org) v2 strict profile): every action it ignores must say *why* (`reject(reason)`), it can't hide bookkeeping state, and it declares its own action/data domains — so the model checker knows exactly what to explore with zero configuration. Several specs are generated independently and vote, so one bad generation doesn't decide the outcome. 3. **Invariants** (`invariants.mjs`) — your rules, as plain JS functions over a state: *"never charged without a confirmed transaction"*, *"an expired session can't accept input."* These encode your **intent**, which is the one thing no tool can derive from the code — code with a bug is a faithful description of the wrong behavior. Then two checks run: **Check 1 — replay (is the spec faithful?).** Real execution traces — captured by wrapping your dispatch/reducer once, so every step logs a `{pre, action, data, post}` window — are replayed against each spec. Before any generated spec is trusted, controls run: a hand-written reference spec must score 100% and a deliberately mutated one must fail, proving the harness can actually tell good from bad. Disagreements are triaged into **spec-errors** (the LLM misread the code), **code-findings** (the code disagrees with an independent reading of itself — investigate), and **contract-errors** (the contract mis-scoped the problem). **polynv grades re-measure under a larger fault model.** 8.0 adds the verdict family (`silence`, `reason-swap`) and the schema family (`schema-weaken`) beside the classic relation four. // Rules the brief requires, over one job's observable state.
const STATUSES = ['none', 'queued', 'running', 'cancelling', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'held'];
const TERMINAL = ['succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'];
const same = (a, b) => a.status === b.status && a.tries === b.tries && a.maxTries === b.maxTries;

export const stateInvariants = [
  { name: 'status-is-known', pred: (s) => STATUSES.includes(s.status) },
  { name: 'absent-job-is-blank', pred: (s) => s.status !== 'none' || (s.tries === 0 && s.maxTries === 0) },
  { name: 'maxTries-1-to-3', pred: (s) => s.status === 'none' || [1, 2, 3].includes(s.maxTries) },
  // "A job is never tried more than its limit."
  { name: 'tries-within-limit', pred: (s) => s.tries >= 0 && s.tries <= s.maxTries },
  // "It fails only when its last try failed."
  { name: 'failed-only-after-last-try', pred: (s) => s.status !== 'failed' || s.tries === s.maxTries },
  { name: 'running-has-a-try', pred: (s) => !['running', 'cancelling', 'succeeded', 'failed'].includes(s.status) || s.tries >= 1 },
];

export const transitionInvariants = [
  // "A refused command changes nothing."
  { name: 'refusal-changes-nothing', pred: (pre, a, d, post, v) => !(v && v.rejected) || same(pre, post) },
  { name: 'terminal-is-final', pred: (pre, a, d, post) => !TERMINAL.includes(pre.status) || same(pre, post) },
  { name: 'maxTries-fixed-after-submit', pred: (pre, a, d, post) => pre.status === 'none' || post.maxTries === pre.maxTries },
  // Only a claim counts a try, and it counts exactly one.
  { name: 'only-claim-counts-a-try', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      a === 'SUBMIT' || post.tries === pre.tries + (a === 'CLAIM' && post.status === 'running' && pre.status === 'queued' ? 1 : 0) },
  // "A cancel never loses the outcome of work already done."
  { name: 'cancelling-finished-ends-succeeded', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'cancelling' && a === 'SUCCEED') || post.status === 'succeeded' },
  { name: 'cancelling-unfinished-ends-cancelled', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'cancelling' && (a === 'FAIL' || a === 'LOST')) || post.status === 'cancelled' },
  { name: 'cancelling-only-from-running-cancel', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'cancelling' || pre.status === 'cancelling' || (pre.status === 'running' && a === 'CANCEL') },
  { name: 'failed-only-from-running-failure', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'failed' || pre.status === 'failed' || (pre.status === 'running' && (a === 'FAIL' || a === 'LOST')) },
  // Change 1: held is entered only from queued by HOLD, left only by RELEASE (to queued) or CANCEL.
  { name: 'held-only-from-queued-hold', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'held' || pre.status === 'held' || (pre.status === 'queued' && a === 'HOLD') },
  { name: 'held-leaves-by-release-or-cancel', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>

      || (a === 'RELEASE' && post.status === 'queued') || (a === 'CANCEL' && post.status === 'cancelled') },
  { name: 'cancel-held-ends-cancelled', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>

// Rules the brief requires, over one job's observable state.
const STATUSES = ['none', 'queued', 'running', 'cancelling', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'held'];
const TERMINAL = ['succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'];
const same = (a, b) => a.status === b.status && a.tries === b.tries && a.maxTries === b.maxTries;

export const stateInvariants = [
  { name: 'status-is-known', pred: (s) => STATUSES.includes(s.status) },
  { name: 'absent-job-is-blank', pred: (s) => s.status !== 'none' || (s.tries === 0 && s.maxTries === 0) },
  { name: 'maxTries-1-to-3', pred: (s) => s.status === 'none' || [1, 2, 3].includes(s.maxTries) },
  // "A job is never tried more than its limit."
  { name: 'tries-within-limit', pred: (s) => s.tries >= 0 && s.tries <= s.maxTries },
  // Change 2: a job may now be failed with tries left, but never without a try.
  { name: 'failed-only-after-a-try', pred: (s) => s.status !== 'failed' || s.tries >= 1 },
  { name: 'running-has-a-try', pred: (s) => !['running', 'cancelling', 'succeeded', 'failed'].includes(s.status) || s.tries >= 1 },
];

export const transitionInvariants = [
  // "A refused command changes nothing."
  { name: 'refusal-changes-nothing', pred: (pre, a, d, post, v) => !(v && v.rejected) || same(pre, post) },
  { name: 'terminal-is-final', pred: (pre, a, d, post) => !TERMINAL.includes(pre.status) || same(pre, post) },
  { name: 'maxTries-fixed-after-submit', pred: (pre, a, d, post) => pre.status === 'none' || post.maxTries === pre.maxTries },
  // Only a claim counts a try, and it counts exactly one.
  { name: 'only-claim-counts-a-try', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      a === 'SUBMIT' || post.tries === pre.tries + (a === 'CLAIM' && post.status === 'running' && pre.status === 'queued' ? 1 : 0) },
  // "A cancel never loses the outcome of work already done."
  { name: 'cancelling-finished-ends-succeeded', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'cancelling' && a === 'SUCCEED') || post.status === 'succeeded' },
  { name: 'cancelling-unfinished-ends-cancelled', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'cancelling' && ['FAIL', 'LOST', 'FAIL_PERMANENTLY'].includes(a)) || post.status === 'cancelled' },
  { name: 'cancelling-only-from-running-cancel', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'cancelling' || pre.status === 'cancelling' || (pre.status === 'running' && a === 'CANCEL') },
  { name: 'failed-only-from-running-failure', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'failed' || pre.status === 'failed'
      || (pre.status === 'running' && ['FAIL', 'LOST', 'FAIL_PERMANENTLY'].includes(a)) },
  // A retryable failure fails the job only on its last try; only a permanent one fails it early.
  { name: 'failed-early-only-if-permanent', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status !== 'failed' && post.status === 'failed' && post.tries < post.maxTries) || a === 'FAIL_PERMANENTLY' },
  { name: 'permanent-failure-of-running-fails', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'running' && a === 'FAIL_PERMANENTLY') || post.status === 'failed' },
  // Change 1: held is entered only from queued by HOLD, left only by RELEASE (to queued) or CANCEL.
  { name: 'held-only-from-queued-hold', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      post.status !== 'held' || pre.status === 'held' || (pre.status === 'queued' && a === 'HOLD') },
  { name: 'held-leaves-by-release-or-cancel', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      pre.status !== 'held' || post.status === 'held'
      || (a === 'RELEASE' && post.status === 'queued') || (a === 'CANCEL' && post.status === 'cancelled') },
  { name: 'cancel-held-ends-cancelled', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'held' && a === 'CANCEL') || post.status === 'cancelled' },
  { name: 'release-held-requeues', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'held' && a === 'RELEASE') || post.status === 'queued' },
  { name: 'retry-when-tries-left', pred: (pre, a, d, post) =>
      !(pre.status === 'running' && (a === 'FAIL' || a === 'LOST') && pre.tries < pre.maxTries) || post.status === 'queued' },
];

export const rejectionInvariants = [
  { name: 'never-submitted-refused', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(s.status === 'none' && a !== 'SUBMIT') || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'duplicate-submit-refused', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(s.status !== 'none' && a === 'SUBMIT') || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'bad-maxTries-refused', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(a === 'SUBMIT' && ![1, 2, 3].includes(d.maxTries)) || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'claim-only-queued', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(a === 'CLAIM' && s.status !== 'queued') || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'finish-only-running-or-cancelling', pred: (s, a, d, v) =>
      !(['SUCCEED', 'FAIL', 'LOST', 'FAIL_PERMANENTLY'].includes(a) && !['running', 'cancelling'].includes(s.status)) || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'cancel-only-queued-held-or-running', pred: (s, a, d, v) =>
      !(a === 'CANCEL' && !['queued', 'held', 'running'].includes(s.status)) || (v && v.rejected) },
  // Change 1: no worker takes a held job.
  { name: 'held-job-not-claimed', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(a === 'CLAIM' && s.status === 'held') || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'hold-only-queued', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(a === 'HOLD' && s.status !== 'queued') || (v && v.rejected) },
  { name: 'release-only-held', pred: (s, a, d, v) => !(a === 'RELEASE' && s.status !== 'held') || (v && v.rejected) },
];

Done: `resubmit` is in place, and polygraph found no invariant violations (9 of 9 tests pass, type-check is clean).

**Implementation**
- `resubmit` turns a failed job back into **queued**, with tries reset to 0 and the same limit. Every other job refuses it.

**Spec and checks (in `spec/`)**
- **Spec and contract:** both now include `RESUBMIT`. A failed job is no longer an end state, so I removed **failed** from the contract's terminal states.
- **Changed invariants:** "an end state never changes" no longer covers failed. "Only a claim changes tries" now allows a resubmit to reset them.
- **New invariants:**
  - A failed job leaves only by `resubmit`, to queued with 0 tries and the same limit.
  - `resubmit` is refused for any job that isn't failed.
- **Model check:** 46 reachable states, no invariant violations.
- **Replay against the code:** the spec agrees with all 3771 recorded steps.

**Capture gaps I found and fixed**
- **Missed states:** resubmission makes cycles possible, so I limited the capture to exploring each (state, command) pair once. My first version of that reached only 18 of the 46 states, because states first met deep in the search got cut off. Exploring breadth-first fixed it.
- **Missing refusals:** capture used to stop at succeeded and cancelled, so refusals from those states were never recorded. It now explores them too.
- **Result:** the corpus covers all 46 states × 15 commands = 690 pairs, which the earlier corpora did not.

**Negative controls:** I added a fourth wrong spec, in which a resubmitted job keeps its used tries. My first version of it accidentally changed `submit` instead of `resubmit`, so it behaved identically to the real spec and the checker passed it. With that fixed, replay flags 708 steps across the four wrong specs. The checker catches each one with 2 to 4 violations. `make.mjs` now refuses a pattern that matches more than once.
